name: freedink
desc: Portable version of the Dink Smallwood game engine
why: Portable Dink Smallwood engine, a cult adventure game with a fan-driven open source community behind it.

brief.what_it_is: GNU FreeDink is a free, portable reimplementation of the game engine for Dink Smallwood, a 2D top-down adventure/RPG similar to classic Zelda. It runs the original game and its fan-made D-Mods with close compatibility, on multiple platforms, and the page says it also runs in a web browser. The project bundles the DFArc front-end for managing and playing D-Mods, and the FreeDinkedit editor for making new adventures. The page does not describe the exact inputs and outputs beyond that.
brief.why_it_exists: The page presents FreeDink as a new, portable version of the Dink Smallwood engine, so the original game and its fan add-ons can run beyond the original platforms. It is also framed as free software under the GPL, with the page noting that free software is more than open source.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internal mechanism. It says the engine runs the original game and D-Mods with close compatibility. For audio, it supports the patent-free Ogg Vorbis format, plus mod, s3m, it, and xm, and says MP3 support may come later.

commands_seen.context: Checks out the source code for the project website itself, not the game. It is listed under a source code note at the bottom of the homepage.

brief.install_notes: The homepage has a 'Get it' section, but I did not follow it, so I have no platform-specific install steps, dependency list, or first-run instructions. The brew description lists four executables: dink, dinkedit, freedink, and freedinkedit. The page says the game also runs in the browser, which may mean no local install is needed for that route.
brief.standout: The engine runs the original game and fan-made D-Mods, some of which are bigger than the original game, and the page says it runs in a browser. The project keeps backward compatibility with D-Mods, so the fan content base is the main reason to use it.
brief.status: Maintained according to the homepage, which says GNU FreeDink is currently maintained by Keiran Harcombe. The page says the main game is finished, with more sounds and translations still being added, and that the engine may evolve but will keep backward compatibility for D-Mods. I did not find a last release date or last commit date, so activity level is only partly confirmed.
brief.caveats: I read only the homepage, not the 'Get it', 'Docs', or 'Links' pages, so install details and platform support are unverified. The homepage has no README in the GitHub sense, so the README-based commands are absent and the one command listed is for the website source. The game is described as close to the original, not exact. MP3 support is not yet available.
quotes: GNU FreeDink is a new and portable version of the game engine, which runs the original game as well as its D-Mods, with close compatibility, under multiple platforms.
The game is so portable that it also runs in your browser!
The main game is finished (except we're adding more sounds as time passes, as well as translations).
